Federal Act of 15 December 2000 on Medicinal Products and Medical Devices (Therapeutic Products Act, TPA)
Loi fédérale du 15 décembre 2000 sur les médicaments et les dispositifs médicaux (Loi sur les produits thérapeutiques, LPTh)
Legge federale del 15 dicembre 2000 sui medicamenti e i dispositivi medici (Legge sugli agenti terapeutici, LATer)

preface.p: English is not an official language of the Swiss Confederation. This translation is provided for information purposes only and has no legal force.

p.docTitle:
Federal Act
on Medicinal Products and Medical Devices

preamble.p: The Federal Assembly of the Swiss Confederation,

based on Articles 95 paragraph 1 and 118 paragraph 2 of the Federal Constitution
SR 101, and having considered the Federal Council Dispatch dated 1 March 1999
BBl 1999 3453,

content.p: The purpose of this Act is to protect human and animal health and to guarantee that only high quality, safe and effective therapeutic products are placed on the market.

blockList.listIntroduction: It shall furthermore:

item.p: protect the consumers of therapeutic products against fraud;
help to ensure that the therapeutic products placed on the market are used in accordance with their purpose and in moderation;
help to ensure that a reliable and well-organised supply of therapeutic products, together with the necessary technical information and advice, is available throughout the country.

blockList.listIntroduction: In the implementation of this Act, in particular in the enactment of the regulations and in the application to an individual case, it must be ensured that:

item.p: the efficiency and independence of the control of therapeutic products is guaranteed in Switzerland;
favourable conditions exist for research and development in the therapeutic product sector;
all players competing in the market fulfil the same legal requirements of safety and quality.

blockList.listIntroduction: This Act applies to:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).
item.p: the handling of medicinal products and medical devices (therapeutic products);

narcotics as defined in the Narcotics Act of 3 October 1951
SR 812.121, insofar as they are used as therapeutic products;
therapeutic treatments, such as gene therapy, insofar as they directly relate to therapeutic products; the Federal Council may enact provisions specific to this subject.

content.p: The Federal Council may completely or partially exempt medical devices intended for use on animals or in veterinary diagnostics from the scope of this Act.

It may make subject to this Act certain products without an intended medical purpose which are comparable to medical devices in terms of functioning and risks profile.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

content.p: For therapeutic products which contain or consist of devitalised human tissues or cells, or derivatives thereof, the Federal Council shall specify requirements for the donation, removal, testing and devitalisation of these tissues or cells.

It may make subject to specific requirements of this Act and of the Transplantation Act of 8 October 2004
SR 810.21 products which contain or consist of devitalised human tissues or cells, or derivatives thereof, and are not therapeutic products, but function as therapeutic products. In addition, it may also specify requirements for the donation, removal, testing and devitalisation of such tissues or cells, or derivatives thereof.

p.span: Human tissue or human cells may only be removed or used for the manufacture of products as specified in paragraphs 1 and 2 if consent has been obtained for removal. For this tissue and these cells, neither financial gain nor any other advantage may be offered, granted, demanded or accepted.

content.p: Any person handling therapeutic products must take all measures necessary according to the state of the art to ensure that human or animal health is not endangered.

The state of the art in science and technology must be considered for complementary medicines without indications, including the principles of the corresponding therapy approach.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: In this Act:

item.p: Medicinal products means products of chemical or biological origin which are intended or claimed to have a medicinal effect on the human or animal organism, in particular in the diagnosis, prevention or treatment of diseases, injuries and handicaps; blood and blood products are also considered to be medicinal products;

item.num:
abis.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: Medicinal products with indications means medicinal products with an officially authorised indication in a specific field of application which are intended for use in accordance with the rules of the medical and pharmaceutical sciences;

item.num:
ater.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: Complementary medicines with indications means medicinal products with an officially authorised indication in a specific field of application which are manufactured according to the manufacturing regulations for complementary therapies such as homeopathy, anthroposophic medicine or traditional Asian medicine and whose field of application is determined according to the principles of the corresponding therapy approach;

aquater.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1). Complementary medicines without indications means complementary medicines without an officially authorised indication in a specific field of application which are intended for use in individual therapies;

aquinquies.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1). Herbal medicines means medicinal products with an authorised indication which exclusively contain one or more herbal substances or herbal preparations and which are not classified as complementary medicines;

asexies.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1). Original preparation means a medicinal product that is authorised by the Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products (Agency) as the first with a specific active substance, including all dosage forms authorised at the same time or later;

asepties.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1). Generic medicinal product means a medicinal product authorised by the Agency which is essentially the same as an original preparation and which is interchangeable with the original preparation due to its identical active substances and its dosage form and dosage;

aocties.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1). Reference preparation means a biological medicinal product that is used in the authorisation documentation for a biosimilar product as a reference for the comparability of its pharmaceutical quality, efficacy and safety;

anovies.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1). Biosimilar product means a biological medicinal product sufficiently similar to a reference preparation authorised by the Agency and that refers to its documentation;

blockList.listIntroduction:
adecies.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1). Important medicinal products intended to treat rare diseases (orphan drugs) means medicinal products for human use for which it has been proven that:

item.p: they are indicated for the diagnosis, prevention or treatment of a life-threatening or chronically debilitating disease affecting no more than five in ten thousand people in Switzerland when the application was submitted, or

they or their active substances are granted the status of Important medicinal products intended to treat rare diseases by another country with an equivalent system of medicinal product control within the meaning of Article 13;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).
item.p: Medical devices means products, including instruments, apparatus, equipment, in vitro diagnostics, software, implants, reagents, materials and other goods or substances which are intended or claimed to have a medical use and whose principal effect is not obtained with a medicinal product;

Manufacture means all stages in the manufacture of a therapeutic product, from the acquisition of the precursors and the processing to the packaging, storage and delivery of the end products, and including the quality controls and batch release;
Placing on the market means the distribution and dispensing of therapeutic products;

item.num:
e.
Amended by Annex No 2 of the FD of 29 Sept. 2017 (Medicrime Convention), in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2018 4771; BBl 2017 3135).
item.p: Distribution means the transfer or release, either free of charge or in return for payment, but not the dispensing, of a therapeutic product and includes the activities of brokers and agents;

Dispensing means the transfer or release, either free of charge or in return for payment, of a ready-to-use therapeutic product destined for use by the purchaser or for use on a third party or on animals;

item.num:
fbis.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: Prescription means the recorded decision of a qualified medical professional issued in accordance with Article 26 paragraph 2 to a specific person, granting that person a right of access to medical services such as care services, medication, analyses or medical devices;
Pharmacopoeia (Pharmacopoeia Europaea and Pharmacopoeia Helvetica) means a collection of regulations on the quality of medicinal products, excipients and certain medical devices;

item.num:
h.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: New active substance means an active substance which is authorised for the first time in Switzerland pursuant to an ordinary procedure under Article 11. Active substances previously only authorised in medicinal products for human use shall be considered new active substances if they are used in products for veterinary use, and vice versa;

item.num:
i.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: Public pharmacy means a pharmacy licensed by the canton, run by a pharmacist, which guarantees regular opening hours and offers direct access to the public;

item.num:
j.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1). Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).
item.p: Hospital pharmacy means a pharmacy in a hospital establishment which is run by a pharmacist and offers, in particular, pharmaceutical services to the customers of the hospital; for the preparation of radiopharmaceuticals in accordance with Article 9 paragraph 2 letter a and paragraph 2bis, an internal radiopharmaceutical establishment is also deemed to be a hospital pharmacy;

item.num:
k.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: Pro-pharmacy means the cantonally approved dispensing of medicinal products in a doctor’s practice or an outpatient healthcare service whose pharmacy is under the professional responsibility of a doctor with a professional licence.

content.p: The Federal Council may, by ordinance, distinguish between the terms used in this Act as well as those used in paragraph 1, define them in greater detail, and may provide for exceptions based upon new findings in science and technology as well as on international developments.

It may, for the area of medical devices, by ordinance, specify different definitions for the terms listed in paragraph 1, provided that this serves the purpose of international harmonisation.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

blockList.listIntroduction:
A licence from the Agency shall be required by those who:
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

item.p: manufacture medicinal products;
add medicinal products to animal feed.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council regulates exemptions from the licence requirement. In particular, it may:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No 1 of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: make the manufacture of medicinal products under Article 9 paragraph 2 letters a–cbis subject to a mandatory cantonal licence or reporting requirement;
exempt from the licence requirement livestock holders who add medicinal products to animal feed intended for their own livestock.

content.p:
It may provide for a licence requirement in accordance with the corresponding internationally recognised requirements for the manufacture of certain categories of pharmaceutical excipients which present an increased risk to patients.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The licence shall be issued if:

item.p: the necessary technical and operational conditions are fulfilled;
an appropriate system of quality assurance exists.

content.p: The competent authority shall verify by inspection that the conditions are fulfilled.

The manufacture of medicinal products and pharmaceutical excipients whose manufacture requires a licence must conform to the recognised rules of good manufacturing practice.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
The Federal Council shall specify the recognised rules of good manufacturing practice. In doing so, it shall take account of internationally recognised guidelines and standards.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: Public pharmacies and public hospitals must hold a manufacturing licence that covers the following:

item.p: public pharmacies: a licence authorising at least the manufacture of medicinal products in accordance with Article 9 paragraph 2 letter a;
hospital pharmacies: a licence authorising at least the manufacture of medicinal products in accordance with Article 9 paragraph 2.

section.heading: Principle for Placing Products on the Market and Authorisation Procedure

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

article.heading: Principle for placing products on the market

content.p: Medicinal products and excipients placed on the market must meet the requirements of the Pharmacopoeia or other pharmacopoeias recognised by the Agency provided that such requirements exist.

Ready-to-use medicinal products and veterinary medicinal products intended for the manufacture of medicinal foodstuffs (premixed medicinal products) may be placed on the market only if authorised by the Agency; the foregoing is without prejudice to international agreements on the recognition of marketing authorisations.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following shall be exempt from authorisation:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No 1 of the FA of 13 June 2008, in force since 1 Oct. 2010 (AS 2008 4873, 2010 4027; BBl 2007 2393).
item.p: medicinal products prepared according to a doctor’s prescription by a public pharmacy or a hospital pharmacy, or under mandate to the latter by another establishment holding a manufacturing licence, and for a given person or group of persons or for a given animal or livestock (magistral formula); on the basis of a prescription, the medicinal product may be manufactured by the public pharmacy or the hospital pharmacy as required or on a small industrial scale but may only be dispensed on a doctor’s prescription;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No 1 of the FA of 13 June 2008, in force since 1 Oct. 2010 (AS 2008 4873, 2010 4027; BBl 2007 2393).
item.p: medicinal products prepared as required or on a small industrial scale by a public pharmacy, a hospital pharmacy, a drugstore or by another establishment holding a manufacturing licence, conforming to a special monograph of the Pharmacopoeia or another pharmacopoeia or a formulary recognised by the Agency, and which are supplied to their own customers (officinal formula);

item.num:
c.
Amended by No 1 of the FA of 13 June 2008, in force since 1 Oct. 2010 (AS 2008 4873, 2010 4027; BBl 2007 2393).
item.p: non-prescription medicinal products prepared as required or on a small industrial scale by a public pharmacy, a hospital pharmacy, a drugstore or by another establishment holding a manufacturing licence, within the limits of the establishment’s right to dispense in compliance with Article 25, according to its own formula or a formula published in the specialised literature, which are intended for dispensing to the establishment's own customers;

cbis.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 13 June 2008, in force since 1 Oct. 2010 (AS 2008 4873, 2010 4027; BBl 2007 2393). medicinal products for which it is proven that there is no authorised or available alternative medicinal product that is applicable and equivalent and which are manufactured in a hospital pharmacy in accordance with the hospital’s own pharmaceuticals list, on a small industrial scale, and are intended for dispensing to its own customers;
medicinal products intended for clinical trials;
medicinal products which cannot be standardised;

item.num:
f.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2018 (AS 2017 2745; BBl 2013 1).

p.inline: medicinal products that were authorised in a canton on 1 January 2002 and which were still on the market when the Amendment of 18 March 2016 came into force; they must be labelled accordingly and may only be placed on the market in the canton concerned and only supplied by persons entitled to supply medicinal products under this Act.

content.p:
An establishment with a manufacturing licence may be commissioned to manufacture medicinal products (contract manufacture) in accordance with paragraph 2 a–cbis.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 13 June 2008 (AS 2008 4873, 2010 4027; BBl 2007 2393). Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

Companies holding a manufacturing licence issued by the Agency may manufacture a complementary medicine for which no alternative and equivalent medicinal product is demonstrably available or authorised, even without a contract manufacturing order in accordance with paragraph 2bis, and market them to companies which are authorised to manufacture these products in accordance with paragraph 2 letters a, b and c. A company may not manufacture more than 100 packages of such a medicinal product with a maximum total of 3,000 daily doses; in the case of homeopathic and anthroposophic medicinal products, this restriction applies to each dilution individually.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 13 June 2008 (AS 2008 4873, 2010 4027; BBl 2007 2393). Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

The Federal Council shall lay down the qualitative and quantitative criteria for the medicinal products manufactured in accordance with paragraphs 2 letters a–cbis and 2bis, and the qualitative criteria for the medicinal products manufactured in accordance with paragraph 2ter.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
The Federal Council may make provision for a requirement of authorisation for the production or manufacturing process used in making medicinal products which cannot be standardised.

…
Repealed by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, with effect from 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Agency may, in accordance with a simplified procedure under Article 14 paragraph 1, temporarily authorise medicinal products for life-threatening or debilitating diseases if:

item.p: they are compatible with the protection of health;
their use is expected to have a major therapeutic benefit; and
no authorised, alternative or equivalent medicinal product is available in Switzerland.

content.p: The Agency shall determine the evidence to be submitted for the evaluation of an application pursuant to paragraph 1.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

article.heading: Temporary authorisation for use and limited placing on the market

content.p: The Agency may temporarily authorise the use of medicinal products referred to in Article 9 paragraph 2 letter d on certain persons or on certain categories of persons outside clinical trials.

blockList.listIntroduction: It may also authorise the temporary or quantitative marketing of a medicinal product to bridge the temporary unavailability of an identical medicinal product authorised in Switzerland, provided that:

item.p: the medicinal product is authorised in another country that has equivalent medicinal product control; and
no essentially identical medicinal product is authorised and available in Switzerland.

article.heading: Conditions for granting a marketing authorisation

blockList.listIntroduction:
Any person applying for a marketing authorisation must:
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: prove that the medicinal products with indications or procedures are of high quality and are safe and effective;

item.num:
abis.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: in the case of complementary medicines without indication, at any time on the basis of documentation:

item.p: prove that they are of high quality, and
credibly demonstrate that the medicinal product in question does not pose a risk to the safety of consumers;
be a holder of an authorisation to manufacture, import or conduct wholesale trade issued by the competent authority;
have a registered address, registered office or a branch office in Switzerland.

content.p: The Agency shall verify that the conditions for granting the marketing authorisation are fulfilled. To this effect, it may carry out product-specific inspections.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The application for a marketing authorisation must contain all of the essential data and documents for its assessment, in particular:

item.p: the name of the medicinal product;
the name of the manufacturer and the distributor;

content.p: c. the manufacturing process, the composition, the quality and the stability of the medicinal product.

blockList.listIntroduction: The application for a marketing authorisation for the following medicinal products must include the information and documents listed below:
Medicinal products with indication:

item.p: the results of physical, chemical, pharmaceutical and biological or microbiological tests,
the results of pharmacological and toxicological tests and clinical trials, including all results from trials in specific population groups,
the therapeutic effects and the undesirable effects,
the labelling, the information supplied about the medicinal product, and the dispensing method and method of administration,
an assessment of the risks and, if necessary, a plan for their systematic recording, investigation and prevention (pharmacovigilance plan),
the paediatric investigation plan referred to in Article 54a;

blockList.listIntroduction: Medicinal products for animals raised for food production:

item.p: the information and documents referred to in letter a,
the detection of residues,
the withdrawal periods.

content.p: In addition to the information and documents referred to in paragraph 1, the application for the authorisation of the processes indicated in Article 9 paragraph 3 must include those referred to in paragraph 2 letter a.
The Agency shall describe the information and the documents referred to in paragraphs 1–3 in greater detail.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council shall stipulate:

item.p: the requirements for organising, carrying out and recording the pharmacological and toxicological tests referred to in paragraph 2 letter a number 2 and the control procedure, taking into account internationally recognised guidelines and standards;
the languages to be used for labelling and information leaflets.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p: The documents relating to a medicinal product containing at least one new active substance and authorised in accordance with Article 11 shall be protected for a period of ten years.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p: If a medicinal product is submitted with one or more known active substances, the corresponding documentation on new indications, modes of administration, dosage forms or dosages, or on its application to a new target animal species shall be protected for a period of three years.

p.inline: For a new indication, this period of protection shall be set by the Agency, on request, at 10 years if it is expected to bring a significant clinical benefit in comparison with existing therapies and if it is backed up by extensive clinical trials.

content.p: On request, the Agency shall grant a ten-year document protection for a medicinal product specifically and exclusively for paediatric use in accordance with the paediatric investigation plan, provided that no document protection exists for another medicinal product authorised by the Agency with the same active substance for the same specific paediatric use.

p.inline: In the case of an important orphan medicinal product, the Agency shall, on request, grant document protection for a period of fifteen years.

content.p: The Federal Council shall regulate the details.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

article.heading: Authorisation of essentially similar medicinal products

blockList.listIntroduction: The application for a marketing authorisation for a medicinal product which is essentially the same as a medicinal product whose documents are protected in accordance with Articles 11a or 11b may be based on the results of the pharmacological, toxicological and clinical tests if:

item.p: the holder of the marketing authorisation for the medicinal product with document protection provides written permission; or
the protection period for the relevant documents has expired.

content.p: If the holder of the marketing authorisation does not agree, the granting of a marketing authorisation for an essentially identical medicinal product shall be permissible at the earliest on the first day after expiry of the period of protection for the medicinal product with document protection. A corresponding application for marketing authorisation may be submitted at the earliest two years before the end of the term of protection.

article.heading: Medicinal products and procedures authorised in foreign countries

content.p: If a medicinal product or procedure is already authorised in a country having equivalent medicinal product control, the results of tests carried out for this purpose shall be taken into account.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Agency shall make provision for simplified procedures for the authorisation of certain categories of medicinal products where this is compatible with the quality, safety and efficacy requirements, and where there is no conflict with Swiss interests or international agreements. In particular, this applies in the case of:

item.p: medicinal products made with known active substances;

item.num:
abis.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: medicinal products whose active substances are used in a medicinal product which, when the application was submitted, has been authorised as a medicinal product for at least 10 years in at least one EU or EFTA country and which is comparable in terms of indications, dosage and method of administration;

item.num:
ater.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: non-prescription medicinal products with indications which, when the application was submitted, have been proven to have been used medically for at least 30 years, and for at least 15 years in EU and EFTA countries;

item.num:
aquater.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: medicinal products which, when the application was submitted, have been authorised as medicinal products for at least 15 years in a canton;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: complementary medicines;

item.num:
c.
Repealed by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, with effect from 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

cbis.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: herbal medicines;

item.num:
d.
Amended by No 1 of the FA of 13 June 2008, in force since 1 Oct. 2010 (AS 2008 4873, 2010 4027; BBl 2007 2393).
item.p: medicinal products prepared by a hospital pharmacy or in the hospital’s own radiopharmaceutical unit for the needs of the hospital;
medicinal products prepared by the army and used in the context of the coordinated army medical corps;
important medicinal products for rare diseases;
veterinary medicinal products, which are intended exclusively for animals not kept for the production of foodstuffs.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Agency shall make provision for a simplified authorisation procedure in the case of an application from another person responsible for the placing on the market of a medicinal product which is already authorised in Switzerland and which is imported from a country with an equivalent authorisation system:

item.p: if the medicinal product satisfies the same requirements as the medicinal product already authorised in Switzerland, in particular in regard to the labelling and the medical information mentioned in Article 11;

if the other person responsible for placing the medicinal product on the market can continue to guarantee that all the authorised medicinal products that he distributes fulfil the same requirements of safety and quality as those of the first applicant.

content.p:
As part of the authorisation procedure for medicinal products that are imported as parallel imports, the Agency shall make provision for simplified rules with regard to labelling and the information supplied about the medicinal product.
Amended by Annex No 1 of the FA of 30 Sept. 2022 (Cost Containment Measures – Package 1b), in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 630; BBl 2019 6071).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

article.heading: Application for a marketing authorisation under the simplified authorisation procedure

blockList.listIntroduction: Applications for a marketing authorisation under the simplified authorisation procedure must contain the following data and documents for the following medicinal products:
Medicinal products referred to in Article 14 paragraph 1 letter abis:

item.p: the data and documents referred to in Article 11 paragraphs 1 and 2 letter a numbers 1–4; the data referred to in Article 11 paragraph 2 letter a number 2 may be replaced by a compilation of equivalent scientific evidence,
proof of the marketing authorisations of the foreign comparator product;

blockList.listIntroduction: Medicinal products referred to in Article 14 paragraph 1letter ater:

item.p: the data and documents referred to in Article 11 paragraphs 1 and 2 letter a numbers 1, 3 and 4,
an assessment of the risks,
proof of 30 or 15 years of medical use;

blockList.listIntroduction: Medicinal products referred to in Article 14 paragraph 1 letter aquater:

item.p: the data and documents referred to in Article 11 paragraphs 1 and 2 letter a numbers 1, 3 and 4,
an assessment of the risks,
the cantonal marketing authorisation;

Medicinal products referred to in Article 14 paragraph 1 letter b: the data and documents referred to in Article 11 paragraphs 1 and 2 letter a; the data referred to in Article 11 paragraph 2 letter a number 2 may be replaced by equivalent data in accordance with specific therapy approaches, in particular by bibliographical evidence of efficacy and safety, or by evidence of use;

Medicinal products referred to in Article 14 paragraph 1 letter cbis: the data and documents referred to in Article 11 paragraphs 1 and 2 letter a; the data referred to in Article 11 paragraph 2 letter a number 2 may be replaced by bibliographical evidence of efficacy and safety, or by evidence of use.

blockList.listIntroduction: Throughout the period of marketing authorisation of medicinal products referred to in paragraph 1 letter a, the following information on the foreign comparator product shall be submitted to the Agency without being requested:

item.p: all internationally recorded safety signals;
all interim reports and final results of the foreign regulatory authority.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

article.heading: Marketing authorisation on the basis of a notification

blockList.listIntroduction: The following may be placed on the market following notification to the Agency:

item.p: complementary medicines without indications, the active substances of which are included in lists for specific therapy approaches;
other medicinal products or groups of medicinal products for which, due to their low risk potential, a simplified marketing authorisation proves to be disproportionate.

content.p: The Agency shall draw up the lists referred to in paragraph 1 letter a. It shall determine the medicinal products or groups of medicinal products referred to in paragraph 1 letter b and regulate the notification procedure.

article.heading:
Authorisation decision and period of the marketing authorisation
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p: The Agency shall grant a marketing authorisation if the conditions are fulfilled. It may attach conditions and requirements to the authorisation.

blockList.listIntroduction: The marketing authorisation is issued for the first time for a period of five years. The Agency shall order a shorter period of authorisation if:

item.p: the authorisations are limited in accordance with Article 9a; or

this is necessary for the protection of health.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p:
The authorisation of medicinal products on the basis of a notification shall be valid for an unlimited period.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

…
Repealed by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, with effect from 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No 1 of the FA of 13 June 2008, in force since 1 Oct. 2010 (AS 2008 4873, 2010 4027; BBl 2007 2393).

article.heading:
Revocation and transfer of the authorisation
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Agency shall revoke the authorisation for a medicinal product if:

item.p: it is not actually placed on the market within three years of the granting of the authorisation;
it is no longer actually on the market during a period of three successive years after it has been placed on the market.

content.p: The Federal Council may provide for exceptions from paragraph 1.

It may provide that, in the case of medicinal products for severe illnesses, injuries or disabilities or of medicinal products with a paediatric indication or for paediatric use, the authorisation is revoked before the period referred to in paragraph 1 has expired. It decides the duration of such periods and lays down the criteria for revocation.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

If the holder of the marketing authorisation intends to cease marketing a medicinal product authorised for a paediatric indication or for paediatric use for which they have obtained protection under Article 11b paragraphs 3 and 4 of this Act or under Article 140n or 140t of the Patents Act of 25 June 1954
SR 232.14, they shall publish that intention in an appropriate form.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

The holder of the marketing authorisation must state in the publication that they will transfer the authorisation documentation to third parties so they can obtain their own authorisation.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p: A marketing authorisation shall be renewed upon application if the authorisation requirements continue to be met.
As a rule, renewed authorisations are valid for an unlimited period. The Agency may, however, limit them, in particular authorisations in accordance with Article 16 paragraph 2 letters a and b.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p: The Agency may review the authorisation at any time; it may adapt or revoke the authorisation in the light of changing circumstances.

If the manufacture of a medicinal product requires special measures to be taken, in particular to guarantee safety, then a release authorisation must be obtained from the Agency for each batch before distribution; the foregoing is without prejudice to international agreements on batch release recognition.
The Agency shall determine the categories of medicinal products for which official batch release is required, as well as procedure and the requirements to be fulfilled.
It shall publish a list of medicinal products which require a batch release for their distribution.

blockList.listIntroduction: A licence granted by the Agency is required by any person who professionally:

item.p: imports ready-to-use medicinal products intended for distribution or dispensing;
exports ready-to-use medicinal products intended for distribution or dispensing;
trades medicinal products in foreign countries from Switzerland, without their entering Switzerland;

acts from Switzerland as a broker or agent for medicinal products.
Amended by Annex No 2 of the FD of 29 Sept. 2017 (Medicrime Convention), in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2018 4771; BBl 2017 3135).

content.p:
The Federal Council shall specify the requirements for activities under paragraph 1.
Amended by Annex No 2 of the FD of 29 Sept. 2017 (Medicrime Convention), in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2018 4771; BBl 2017 3135).

blockList.listIntroduction: It may issue exemptions from the requirement of licence for:

item.p: medical professionals who work across borders;
international organisations.

content.p:
Goods stored in a customs warehouse or a bonded warehouse shall be considered to be imported.
Inserted by Annex No 17 of the Customs Act of 18 March 2005, in force since 1 May 2007 (AS 2007 1411; BBl 2004 567).
The Federal Council may issue special regulations for goods in transit.
If another State requests export certificates and attestations for the importing of medicinal products, the Agency may issue such documents to persons holding an authorisation to export.

blockList.listIntroduction: The licence shall be issued if:

item.p: the necessary technical and operational conditions are fulfilled;
an appropriate system of quality assurance exists.

content.p: The licence shall also be issued to the applicant who already possesses a manufacturing licence for medicinal products. Furthermore, the licence referred to in Article 18 paragraphs 1 letters b and c shall be issued to the applicant already possessing a licence for the import or wholesale trade of medicinal products.
The competent authority shall verify by inspection that the conditions are fulfilled.
Medicinal products which have been authorised, or which are not subject to authorisation, may be imported.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council may permit the importing of small quantities of non-authorised ready-to-use medicinal products by:

item.p: private individuals for their personal use;
medical professionals.

content.p:
It may allow unauthorised, ready-to-use, non-prescription medicinal products for which no alternative and equivalent medicinal product has been authorised to be imported in small quantities in accordance with Article 25 paragraph 1 letters b and c within the limits of their dispensing authority.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: It may:

item.p: stipulate that the licence to import certain medicinal products requiring a specific control for the protection of health be granted in particular cases by the Agency;
restrict or prohibit the importing of certain medicinal products if circumstances suggest that they could be intended for illegal purposes or misuse.

content.p: The Agency shall draw up a list of medicinal products for which imports shall be restricted or prohibited.

article.heading: Restrictions on export and foreign trade

blockList.listIntroduction: The export of medicinal products and their foreign trade from Switzerland shall be prohibited if:

item.p: they are prohibited in the target country;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: circumstances suggest that they are intended for illegal purposes; or

item.num:
c.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: it is deemed that they are intended for capital punishment.

content.p:
The Federal Council shall regulate the requirements for the export and foreign trade of medicinal products which could be used for capital punishment. It shall take account of the EU provisions.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

The Federal Council may stipulate that in particular cases the export of medicinal products which are not authorised in Switzerland or in the target country is prohibited by the Agency or subject to restrictions.
The Agency shall draw up a list of medicinal products for which export shall be restricted or prohibited.
In particular cases, it may grant exemptions from export restrictions or bans, in particular if the authority of the target country agrees to the import.

article.heading: Duties of diligence at the time of export

content.p: Any person exporting ready-to-use medicinal products, whether pre-packaged or not, should provide the recipient, without being asked, with the appropriate basic medical and pharmaceutical information.
Any person exporting medicinal products intended for use in clinical trials must demand proof that the rules of good clinical trial practice are applied.

section.heading:
Distribution, Prescription, Dispensing and Application
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p: Medicinal products shall be classified into categories according to whether or not they are subject to prescription.

A category of over-the-counter medicinal products shall be created for which neither medical and pharmaceutical nor professional customer advice is required. Articles 24–27 and 30 do not apply to this category.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

The Federal Council shall lay down the classification criteria.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

article.heading: Allocation of the medicinal products to the individual categories

content.p: The Agency shall categorise each medicinal product for which it has granted a marketing authorisation in accordance with the criteria laid down by the Federal Council. It shall take into account the professional competence of the professional groups entitled to dispense medicinal products.
It shall review the categorisation of medicinal products periodically or at the request of the holder of the marketing authorisation and adapt it to the state of the art in science and technology.

article.heading: Dispensing of medicinal products subject to prescription

blockList.listIntroduction: The following persons shall be entitled to dispense prescription-only medicinal products:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: pharmacists, on presentation of a doctor’s prescription. They may dispense medicinal products without a doctor’s prescription if they have direct contact with the person concerned, if they document the product dispensed, and if:

item.p: the medicinal products and indications have been designated by the Federal Council, or
the case is justified and exceptional;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: all other medical professionals in accordance with the provisions on pro-pharmacy and taking account of Article 1 paragraph 3 letter c;

content.p: c. all duly trained professionals, under the supervision of a person specified in letters a and b.

The Federal Council shall determine the form and the scope of the documentation obligation pursuant to paragraph 1 letter a.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

Prescription-only medicated foodstuffs for animals may also, on presentation of a prescription from a veterinary surgeon, be dispensed by persons licensed to add medicinal products to animal foodstuffs.
The cantons may license the persons referred to in Article 25 paragraph 1 letter c, to use certain prescription-only medicinal products.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following shall be entitled to dispense non-prescription medicinal products:

item.p: persons entitled to dispense prescription medicinal products;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: druggist holding a federal diploma;
all other duly trained persons, within the limits of their right to dispense medicinal products;
all duly trained professionals, under the supervision of persons referred to in letters a and b.

content.p: The Federal Council shall determine the categories of duly trained persons which are referred to in paragraph 1 letter c.

The Agency shall determine the medicinal products which may be dispensed by the persons referred to in paragraph 1 letter c.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

…
Repealed by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, with effect from 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

Subject to the provisions of paragraphs 2 and 3, the cantons may grant to persons holding a qualification recognised by the canton the right to dispense certain groups of medicinal products, such as those pertaining to complementary medicine. The Agency must be informed of this.

article.heading:
Principle of prescription, dispensing and application
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p:
The recognised rules of pharmaceutical and medical sciences must be respected when prescribing, dispensing and using medicinal products, and the principles of the corresponding therapy approach must be respected when prescribing, dispensing and using complementary medicines without indications. The Federal Council may specify these rules in more detail.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
A medicinal product may only be prescribed if the state of health of the consumer or patient is known.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following principles and minimum requirements must be observed for the prescription of medicinal products:

item.p: The prescription meets the minimal requirements set by the Federal Council following consultations with the medical professions concerned.

The prescription shall become the property of the person for whom it was issued. The person should remain free to decide whether to receive the prescribed product or to obtain a second opinion and to determine with which authorised provider they want to redeem the prescription. In the case of electronic prescriptions, the choice of provider should not be restricted by technical obstacles.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019, let. a in force since 1 Jan. 2020 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p:
The prescriber shall not influence patients in the choice of the person who supplies them with the medicinal products if he or she derives a material benefit from doing so. The Federal Council may provide for exceptions.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

Before a prescription-only medicinal product for human use is dispensed, a person authorised to prescribe and dispense the product must in principle issue a prescription to the patient. The patient may decline to accept the prescription.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
In principle, mail-order trade in medicinal products is prohibited.

blockList.listIntroduction: A licence may only be issued under the following conditions:

item.p: there is a doctor’s prescription for the medicinal product;
no safety requirements oppose it;
appropriate consultation is guaranteed;
sufficient medical supervision of the effect of the medicinal product is guaranteed.

content.p: The Federal Council shall regulate the details.
The cantons shall issue the authorisation.
Any person engaged in the wholesale trade of medicinal products must possess a licence issued by the Agency.

blockList.listIntroduction: The licence shall be issued if:

item.p: the necessary technical and operational conditions are fulfilled;
an appropriate system of quality assurance exists.

content.p: The licence shall also be issued if the applicant already possesses a manufacturing or import licence for medicinal products.
The competent authority shall verify by inspection that the conditions are fulfilled.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex No 2 of the FD of 29 Sept. 2017 (Medicrime Convention), in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2018 4771; BBl 2017 3135).

content.p: Any person engaged in the wholesale trade of medicinal products must respect the recognised principles of good distribution practice.
The Federal Council shall specify the recognised principles of good distribution practice. In doing so, it shall take account of internationally recognised guidelines and standards.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2020 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

content.p: Any person dispensing medicinal products must possess a cantonal licence.
The licence shall be issued when the required specialist conditions are met and there is a quality assurance system in place which is appropriate for the type and size of the establishment.
The cantons may issue further requirements. They regulate the mandatory licensing process and carry out periodical inspections of retail establishments and practices.

blockList.listIntroduction: In principle, it shall be permitted to:

item.p: advertise all types of medicinal products if the advertising is directed exclusively at persons who prescribe or dispense them;
advertise non-prescription medicinal products to the general public.

content.p: The Federal Council shall lay down the conditions for the publication of price comparisons for prescription medicinal products.

It may, in order to protect health and prevent fraud, restrict or prohibit the advertising of certain medicinal products or groups of medicinal products and enact regulations concerning cross-border advertising.

blockList.listIntroduction: Advertising shall be deemed unlawful:

item.p: if it is misleading or contrary to public order and morality;
if it may incite an excessive, abusive or inappropriate use of medicinal products;

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).
item.p: if it is for medicinal products which may not be placed on the market nationally or cantonally.

blockList.listIntroduction: Advertising directed at the general public shall be deemed unlawful for medicinal products which:

item.p: may only be supplied on a prescription;

contain narcotic or psychotropic substances as referred to in the Narcotics Act of 3 October 1951
SR 812.121;
may not, on account of their composition and their intended use, be used without the intervention of a doctor for the necessary diagnosis, prescription or treatment;
are frequently the object of abuse or which lead to an addiction or dependence.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, with effect from 1 Jan. 2020 (AS 2017 2745, 2019 1393; BBl 2013 1).

section.heading: Special Provisions on Blood and Blood Products

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 29 Sept. 2023 (Amendments to the Provisions on Blood Donation), in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 534; BBl 2022 2348, 3169).

article.heading: Ban on payment for blood donations

content.p: It is prohibited to offer, grant, claim or accept a financial gain or other advantage in exchange for a human blood donation.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following are not regarded as a financial gain or other advantage:

item.p: compensation for any loss of earnings or expenses directly incurred by the donor;
damages for any injury sustained by the donor as a result of the blood donation;
a subsequent symbolic gesture of gratitude.

content.p: Any person drawing blood from persons for the purpose of transfusion or the manufacture of therapeutic products or for supply to a third party must possess an operating licence issued by the Agency.

blockList.listIntroduction: The licence shall be issued if:

item.p: the necessary technical and operational conditions are fulfilled;
an appropriate system of quality assurance exists.

content.p: The Agency shall verify by inspection that the licensing conditions are fulfilled.

Establishments such as hospitals which only stock blood or blood products must possess a cantonal operating licence. The cantons shall lay down the conditions and the procedure for granting this licence. They shall carry out periodical inspections.
An import licence is required for each individual batch of imported blood and blood products. Storage in a customs warehouse shall be deemed to be importing.

Blood and labile blood products imported for transfusions must meet the requirements of the ban on payment for blood donations specified in Article 33a.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 29 Sept. 2023 (Amendments to the Provisions on Blood Donation), in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 534; BBl 2022 2348, 3169).
The Federal Council may make provision for exemptions from an import licence if all danger to persons is excluded.

article.heading: Fitness of the donor to give blood

content.p: The holder of the licence referred to in Article 34 paragraph 1 must verify that the donor is fit to give blood.

blockList.listIntroduction: Persons excluded from donating blood shall be those:

item.p: whose health could suffer from the extraction of blood;
whose blood may transmit pathogens.

content.p:
The exclusion criteria must not discriminate against anyone. Insofar as the criteria are linked to the risk behaviour of persons who are willing to donate, they shall relate to individual behaviour and must be scientifically justified.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 29 Sept. 2023 (Amendments to the Provisions on Blood Donation), in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 534; BBl 2022 2348, 3169).

The Federal Council shall lay down the requirements relating to the donor’s fitness to give blood, the competence to establish this fitness and the data which must be recorded at the time of the blood donation.

article.heading: Rules of good manufacturing practice in the handling of blood and blood products

content.p: Any operations relating to blood and labile blood products, in particular the extraction, manufacture, processing, storage and the placing on the market, must be conducted in accordance with the principles of quality management and the recognised principles of good manufacturing practice in the handling of blood and blood products.
Blood and labile blood products as well as associated blood samples must be labelled such that they can be unambiguously identified at any time.
The Federal Council shall specify the recognised rules of good manufacturing practice. In doing so, it shall take account of internationally recognised guidelines and standards.
Donated blood must be tested for the presence or signs of pathogens and examinations must be carried out in order to guarantee compatibility.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council shall specify:

item.p: for which pathogens or which signs of their presence the blood should be tested;
the procedure to be followed when a test result is positive;
the examinations to be carried out in order to guarantee compatibility;
the regulations concerning the execution of tests.

content.p: It may grant exemptions to the obligation to test in the case of autologous transfusions.

blockList.listIntroduction: Any person handling blood or blood products must:

item.p: record all of the processes which are important for safety;
maintain the records in such a manner as to be able to trace the data back to the person who donated or received the blood;

blockList.listIntroduction: For each extraction of blood, the following shall in particular be recorded:

item.p: the surname, first name and the date of birth of the blood donor;
the date on which the blood was taken;
the test results and their interpretation.

blockList.listIntroduction: For a person excluded from donating blood, the following shall be recorded:

item.p: the surname, first name and the date of birth;
the date and the reasons for exclusion.

blockList.listIntroduction: For a person to whom blood or blood products are to be administered, the following shall be recorded:

item.p: the surname, first name and the date of birth;
the date of administration;
the labelling and the origin of the blood or blood products.

content.p: The Federal Council shall regulate the details. In particular, it may grant exemptions from the obligation to record in the case of autologous blood donations.

The information recorded under Article 39 and all important documents must be archived for 30 years.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council shall regulate the details. In particular, it may:

item.p: make provision for the transfer to the Agency, or the archiving, of the records referred to in Article 39 and any important documents, should the establishment cease its activity prior to the expiry of the archiving period;
grant exemptions from the obligation to archive in the case of autologous transfusions.

article.heading:
Further safety provisions
Amended by No I of the FA of 29 Sept. 2023 (Amendments to the Provisions on Blood Donation), in force since 1 Jan. 2025 (AS 2024 534; BBl 2022 2348, 3169).

content.p: The Federal Council may prescribe additional safety precautions; in particular it may determine that the procedures for the removal or the inactivation of possible pathogens may only be applied after the Agency has given authorisation.

section.heading: Special Provisions on Veterinary Medicinal Products

content.p: A medicinal product may only be prescribed or supplied for an animal if the prescriber knows the animal or livestock.
If the medicinal product is intended for production animals, the prescriber must also know the state of health of the animal.

The Federal Council may prohibit the prescription and dispensing of medicinal products or the application of medicinal products that need no authorisation in accordance with Article 9 paragraph 2 for production animals. It may also restrict the prescription, dispensing or application of these products.
Amended by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council may provide for measures to reduce antimicrobial resistance, in particular:

item.p: measures to reduce antibiotic consumption and promote animal health;
requirements for the training and further education of veterinarians and livestock holders.

content.p: It may also restrict or prohibit the use of certain antibiotic agents in veterinary medicine in accordance with foreign regulations if this appears necessary for the effective treatment of patients.

Any person who imports or exports, distributes or dispenses veterinary medicinal products or administers or allows them to be administered to production animals must keep a record of incomings and outgoings of such medicinal products and archive the supporting documents.
The Federal Council may impose measures for enforcement on the cantons and oblige them to inform the competent federal office of the enforcement measures taken and the test results.

A medical device used in accordance with its intended use must not endanger the health of the user, the consumer, the patient or a third party. The intended performance must be demonstrated.
Second sentence amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).
Any person placing a medical device on the market must be able to prove that the device satisfies the fundamental requirements.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council shall lay down the requirements that medical devices must satisfy. In particular it shall lay down:

item.num:
a
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1)..
item.p: the fundamental safety and performance requirements;
the rules of their classification;
the languages used for the product information;

item.num:
d.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).
item.p: the product labelling.

content.p:
The Agency shall, in consultation with the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, designate technical standards and common specifications which are appropriate for giving concrete form to the fundamental requirements. It shall designate, as far as possible, internationally harmonised standards. It shall publish in the Federal Gazette the titles of the designated technical standards and common specifications, also indicating the references or where they may be obtained.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).
The Federal Council shall lay down the requirements for medical devices intended for use in clinical trials.

It may provide for the relaxation of requirements for medical devices produced and used only within health institutions.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

It may provide for the permissibility of reprocessing and further use of single-use devices. It shall specify the relevant conditions.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).
Any person placing a medical device on the market must be able to prove that it has been submitted to the prescribed procedures for assessing conformity.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council shall regulate the prescribed procedures for assessing conformity. In particular it shall lay down:

item.p: the types of procedures;
the medical devices for which an authority for assessing conformity must be enlisted;
the documents required and the length of time for which they should be archived.

blockList.listIntroduction: It may:

item.p: require clinical trials for certain medical devices, which will form an integral part of the proof of conformity;

permit exemptions from the conformity assessment for certain medical devices or medical device groups.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Aug. 2020 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

content.p: The manufacturer must register medical devices in the information system specified in Article 62c or in the European database on medical devices (Eudamed). It must also ensure that a unique device identifier is assigned to the medical device.
The Federal Council shall define the modalities for registration and for device identification. It may provide for exemptions from the obligations specified in paragraph 1.

It may regulate the obligations incumbent on the other economic operators concerned and on health institutions in connection with registration and device identification. It may, in particular, provide for an obligation to record and store the unique device identifiers of the devices acquired or supplied in certain categories.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following are deemed to be economic operators:

item.p: the manufacturers;
the persons authorised to represent manufacturers with headquarters abroad (authorised representatives);
the importers;
the distributors;
the natural and legal persons who combine medical devices in order to place them on the market in the form of a system or a procedure pack;
the natural and legal persons who sterilise devices as specified in letter e before they are placed on the market.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

content.p: The manufacturer must produce technical documentation.

The technical documentation must be such as to permit an assessment of the conformity of the medical device with the requirements of this Act. In particular, it shall also contain information and data on post-market surveillance.
The manufacturer must keep the technical documentation up to date.
The Federal Council shall specify for what medical devices what data and information must be included in the technical documentation, and how this documentation must be made available.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

content.p: The manufacturer must establish and maintain a quality management system which is appropriate to the risk class and type of medical device and ensures compliance with the requirements of this Act.
The quality management system shall include, in particular, a risk management system and a post-market surveillance system.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The economic operators shall disclose to the competent authority, on request:

item.p: all economic operators from whom they have acquired a medical device;
all economic operators to whom they have supplied a medical device;
all health institutions or health professionals to whom they have supplied a medical device.

content.p: The Federal Council shall specify for how long the information has to be kept.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

content.p: The manufacturer or the authorised representative must have sufficient financial coverage to compensate for damage caused by defective medical devices.
The authorised representative shall be jointly and severally liable with the manufacturer vis-à-vis the injured party.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council may:

item.p: make provision for mandatory notification for the placing on the market of certain medical devices;
make provision for mandatory licensing for the placing on the market of certain medical devices, in particular for in vitro diagnostics;
make provision for an obligation for economic operators and conformity assessment bodies to use Eudamed or the information system specified in Article 62c.

blockList.listIntroduction: It shall regulate:

item.p: the additional obligations of economic operators and health institutions, in particular concerning the registration of the manufacturers and the information to be provided in connection with implantable medical devices;
the requirements for the manufacturers’ and authorised representatives’ persons responsible for regulatory compliance, and their other obligations.

blockList.listIntroduction: For the protection of health, the Federal Council may, for certain medical devices:

item.p: make provision that they can only be dispensed on a medical prescription;
lay down the necessary technical and operational conditions or a mandatory notification for their dispensing and use;
attach to the dispensing of products the condition that the devices concerned must be traceable between their manufacture and their use and vice versa.

content.p:
Article 26 applies by analogy to medical devices.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 18 March 2016, in force since 1 Jan. 2019 (AS 2017 2745, 2018 3575; BBl 2013 1).

Any person who uses a medical device commercially or who uses it on a third party shall be obliged to take all the necessary measures for the maintenance of such device to ensure the continued performance and the safety of the medical device.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council may:

item.p: specify the type of maintenance required for certain medical devices or certain classes of medical devices;
regulate the procedure for proving that the obligation of maintenance and the relative requirements have been fulfilled;
make the maintenance dependent upon the technical conditions.

content.p: If required for the protection of health, the Federal Council may restrict or prohibit the import or export of certain medical devices.

If another state requests export certificates and attestations for medical devices which are to be imported, the Agency may, on request, issue these documents to the manufacturer or to the authorised representative with a registered office in Switzerland.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

Any person exporting a medical device to a state with which Switzerland has concluded an agreement under international law for the mutual recognition of conformity assessments and procedures for medical devices must be able to demonstrate that the fundamental requirements referred to in Article 45 paragraph 2 are fulfilled.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).
The Federal Council may, in order to protect health and prevent fraud, restrict or prohibit the advertising of certain medical devices and enact regulations concerning cross-border advertising.

chapter.heading: Common Provisions on Medicinal Products and Medical Devices

content.p: The Agency shall publish the Pharmacopoeia.
It shall involve the interested parties in the drafting of the Pharmacopoeia. In particular, it shall call upon experts and working groups.

It shall participate in the development of the European Pharmacopoeia (Pharmacopoeia Europaea) in accordance with international conventions and transpose it into federal law. It may enact additional regulations valid for Switzerland (Pharmacopoeia Helvetica).

The Pharmacopoeia shall be published separately from the Official Compilation of Federal Legislation. The Federal Council shall regulate the details of publication and in particular shall stipulate the languages in which it shall be published.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex No 6 of the Human Research Act of 30 Sept. 2011, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 3215; BBl 2009 8045).

content.p:
For clinical trials of therapeutic products in humans, the Human Research Act of 30 September 2011
SR 810.30 applies in addition to the provisions of this Act.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex No 6 of the Human Research Act of 30 Sept. 2011, in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 3215; BBl 2009 8045).

content.p: Clinical trials of therapeutic products require authorisation from the Agency in advance.

Exempted from mandatory authorisation are clinical trials involving authorised medicinal products used in accordance with the product information.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council may:

item.p: for other trials, grant an exemption from mandatory authorisation or specify mandatory notification;
for clinical trials of veterinary therapeutic products, specify mandatory authorisation or notification;

item.num:
c.

item.p: make modifications to clinical trials subject to mandatory authorisation.

blockList.listIntroduction: As part of the authorisation procedure, the Agency shall verify:

item.p: in the case of medicinal products, whether they comply with the rules of Good Manufacturing Practice and of medicinal product safety;

blockList.listIntroduction: in the case of medical devices, whether:

item.p: the medical devices meet the requirements specified in Article 45, insofar as compliance with these requirements is not the subject of the clinical trial,
the risks associated with a medical device are duly considered in the clinical trial,

the information on the medical device is in line with current scientific knowledge and is correctly indicated in the protocol.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).

Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 26 May 2021 (AS 2020 2961; BBl 2019 1).
